section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > abstract
text: Leveler is one of the most important additives for super-conformal copper electroplating, which has been widely applied in the fabrication of nanoscale (or microscale) interconnect features in integrated circuits (ICs) and printed circuit boards (PCBs). Because the structure-property relationship of the leveler is not clear, the development of novel leveler with high microvia filling performance is very time-consuming and challenging.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > abstract
text: Because the structure-property relationship of the leveler is not clear, the development of novel leveler with high microvia filling performance is very time-consuming and challenging. In this study, a series of triphenylmethane-based (TPM-based) molecules with different nitrogen-containing groups have been designed, synthesized, and investigated as novel levelers for superconformal copper electroplating. Their structure-property relationships are investigated by electrochemical analyses, contact angle measurements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > abstract
text: Their structure-property relationships are investigated by electrochemical analyses, contact angle measurements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments. It is found that the steric hindrance and the type of the nitrogen-containing groups (tertiary amine or quaternary ammonium with counter anions) in a leveler not only affect its adsorption ratio and strength on the copper interface, but also affect its adsorption preference on different copper crystalline plane.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > abstract
text: It is found that the steric hindrance and the type of the nitrogen-containing groups (tertiary amine or quaternary ammonium with counter anions) in a leveler not only affect its adsorption ratio and strength on the copper interface, but also affect its adsorption preference on different copper crystalline plane. In combination with Cl−, polyethylene glycol (PEG, suppressor), and bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS, accelerator), all TPM-based levelers show excellent microvia filling performances in copper electroplating and their effective concentrations are related to their antagonistic ability against the accelerator SPS.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: Copper electrochemical deposition (ECD) for trench and microvia filling as interconnects in integrated circuits (ICs) or printed circuit boards (PCBs) is one of the most important techniques in modern electronic manufacturing industry [1,2]. For better stability and reliability, the ECD copper in these nanoscale and microscale interconnect features are required to be void-free. Therefore, a technology named “super-conformal” or “bottom-up” copper electroplating has been developed and widely applied in industrial practice.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: Therefore, a technology named “super-conformal” or “bottom-up” copper electroplating has been developed and widely applied in industrial practice. The electroplating process was carried out in an acid copper electrolyte, which was composed of copper sulfate, sulfuric acid, chloride, and trace organic additives. Though the organic additives’ amounts in the electrolytes are very small (generally at several parts per million), the additives play a crucial role in the super-conformal electroplating.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: Though the organic additives’ amounts in the electrolytes are very small (generally at several parts per million), the additives play a crucial role in the super-conformal electroplating. The competitive adsorption and differential distribution of the additives on the cathode surface are the origination for the realization of “bottom-up” copper filling electroplating. According to the additives’ different electrochemical effects in the electroplating, the additives were categorized as accelerators, suppressors, and levelers, respectively.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: According to the additives’ different electrochemical effects in the electroplating, the additives were categorized as accelerators, suppressors, and levelers, respectively. Bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS) [3,4] and its reduced monomer sodium 3-mercapto-1-propanesulfonate (MPS) [5,6] are most widely used accelerators. In electroplating, the accelerators can reduce the cathodic polarization and facilitate the copper reduction [7,8]. The suppressors are usually polyether compounds, such as polyethylene glycol (PEG) [9,10], polypropylene glycol (PPG) [11,12], or their copolymers [13,14].

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: The suppressors are usually polyether compounds, such as polyethylene glycol (PEG) [9,10], polypropylene glycol (PPG) [11,12], or their copolymers [13,14]. In contrast to the accelerators, the suppressors synergistically work with chloride ions to increase the cathodic polarization and thus suppress the copper reduction. Leveler is another important additive used in the electrolyte to fulfill the super-conformal electroplating, which usually are nitrogencontaining molecules and positively charged in the acid electroplating solution.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: Leveler is another important additive used in the electrolyte to fulfill the super-conformal electroplating, which usually are nitrogencontaining molecules and positively charged in the acid electroplating solution. As reported, the levelers can adsorb at the highdensity charge region of the cathode to inhibit the copper deposition and level the copper surface [15]. In addition, the use of a leveler in the microvia filling electroplating solution can greatly expand the application concentration range of accelerators [16].

text: Currently, most of the reported levelers are nitrogen-containing dyes, such as the Janus Green B (JGB) [17], Alcian Blue (ABPV) [18,19], and Diazine Black (DB)[16] etc., or non-dye heterocyclic aromatic molecules, such as 2-amino-4-methylbenzothiazole (AMBT)[20] and 2-mercaptopyridine (2-MP)[21,22] etc. Because the structure-property relationship of the leveler is not clear yet, the development of novel leveler with high microvia filling performance is very time-consuming and challenging.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: To further investigate the structural influence of nitrogencontaining groups on their electrochemical properties and microvia filling performance, a series of novel TPM-based molecules with different nitrogen-containing functional groups were designed and synthesized. As shown in Fig. 1, TPM-1 and TPM-3 are tertiary amines with pyrrolidine and piperidine as the nitrogen-containing groups, respectively. TPM-2, TPM-4, and TPM-5 are quaternary ammoniums, in which TPM-2 and TPM-5 were methylated base on TPM-1 with I− and Cl− as the counter anions, respectively, and TPM-4 was methylated from TPM-3.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 1. Introduction
text: TPM-2, TPM-4, and TPM-5 are quaternary ammoniums, in which TPM-2 and TPM-5 were methylated base on TPM-1 with I− and Cl− as the counter anions, respectively, and TPM-4 was methylated from TPM-3. In this study, the TPM-based molecules were used as levelers in the super-conformal copper electroplating and their structure-property relationship were carefully investigated by electrochemical analyses, contact angle measurements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 4. Conclusions
text: In this study, a series of novel triphenylmethane-based molecules (TPM-2 to TPM-5) with varied nitrogen-containing functional groups were synthesized and investigated as levelers for copper super-conformal electroplating. The structure-property relationships of the TPM-based levelers have been studied in detail with electrochemical analyses, surface activity measurements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 4. Conclusions
text: The structure-property relationships of the TPM-based levelers have been studied in detail with electrochemical analyses, surface activity measurements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments. It was found that all TPM-based levelers show inhibition effect in the copper electroplating and their antagonistic ability against SPS followed in the order of TPM-2 TPM-4 TPM-1 TPM-3 TPM-5. The inhibition ability of the TPM-based levelers positively correlated to their adsorption ratio on the copper interface.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 4. Conclusions
text: The inhibition ability of the TPM-based levelers positively correlated to their adsorption ratio on the copper interface. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that the strongest inhibition effect of TPM-2 and TPM-4 was caused by the synergist interaction of the TPMbased structures and the counter ion I−; the replacement of a fivemembered pyrrolidine ring (TPM-1) by a six-membered piperidine ring (TPM-2) leads to a decrease of the leveler’s inhibition ability; the quaternization of a tertiary amine (TPM-1) with Cl− Cl^- as the counter ion leads a much weaker antagonistic effect against SPS (TPM-5).

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 4. Conclusions
text: Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that the strongest inhibition effect of TPM-2 and TPM-4 was caused by the synergist interaction of the TPMbased structures and the counter ion I−; the replacement of a fivemembered pyrrolidine ring (TPM-1) by a six-membered piperidine ring (TPM-2) leads to a decrease of the leveler’s inhibition ability; the quaternization of a tertiary amine (TPM-1) with Cl− Cl^- as the counter ion leads a much weaker antagonistic effect against SPS (TPM-5). Based on the results, it can be concluded that the minor adjustment of the nitrogen-containing group’s structures in a leveler has a significant impact on its electrochemical properties and microvia filling performance.

section: Structural influence of nitrogen-containing groups on triphenylmethane-based levelers in super-conformal copper electroplating > 4. Conclusions
text: Based on the results, it can be concluded that the minor adjustment of the nitrogen-containing group’s structures in a leveler has a significant impact on its electrochemical properties and microvia filling performance. The steric hindrance and the type (tertiary amine or quaternary ammonium with counter anions) of the nitrogen-containing groups need to be comprehensively considered when one designs new levelers for the super-conformal copper electroplating.
